dedupe_keys.name: optiflow flexible network flow modelling framework for energy systems

description: OptiFlow is a generalised spatio-temporal network optimisation model with partial equilibrium and a bottom-up approach, coded in GAMS and developed at the Technical University of Denmark. It represents linear flows across processes, space and time, including transport, inter-temporal storage and processes with time delay, and can model network topologies of energy carriers and feedstocks. It runs alone or hard-linked with the Balmorel energy system model, and has been applied to waste management, biomass, renewable fuel production, Power-to-X and cascading hydropower. The Zenodo record of March 2025, by Rasmus Bramstoft, Frederik Fristed, Amalia Pizarro Alonso, Theis Utoft Madsen, Marie Münster and Hans Ravn, holds the model and data for a case study linking OptiFlow with Balmorel to optimise renewable maritime fuel production, and supports the article published in Energy in 2026. Coverage is set by the user; the case study is European. The code is accessible on GitHub and Zenodo under the ISC licence at no cost. Caveats: GAMS is required, and the GitHub README points to the Balmorel community for the latest development. Simulation uses are supply chain and network design for fuels, hydrogen and waste-to-energy coupled with the power system. Related records: model-balmorel-energy-system-model is the linked energy system model.
